newsitem.title: UK: GKN shares gain as results meet forecasts.
newsitem.headline: GKN shares gain as results meet forecasts.

text.p: Shares in engineering group GKN Plc were higher on Thursday after the company reported annual pre-tax profits of 362.8 million stg and said it expected to see an improvement in 1997 for its automotive businesses.
The shares were up 21-1/2p at 977p by 1132 GMT.
"They were good results...very solid." said Merrill Lynch industry analyst Adam Collins, after returning from the company's results briefing.

"The auto performance was very resilient," he said. "In a difficult market place, growing profits was an achievement. Likewise aerospace and Chep, which now make up about 46 percent of the group, continue to grow strongly and will be the real growth driver behind the business."
Collins said he was making no material changes to his earnings forecasts for the group but added that he remains positive on the stock.
"The rating is quite low on these shares, they have been oversold following the Meineke dispute," he said.

The company said it had made no provision for the on-going litigation against its U.S. franchise Meineke Discount Muffler Shops, because no decision against the company had yet been made and the group would have a strong case for appeal in that event.

"For the year ahead the auto businesses will again face difficult trading conditions but will have a favourable geographic mix," Collins said. "There are also potential productivity improvement and the other two businesses are on a growth track which should continue."
Among the negatives for the group's share-price Collins noted that the delivery profile at Westland will be flat over the next two years before jumping sharply in 1998.
The analyst commented that the worries over a possible new entrant in the pallet market may have been overdone.
"There is also the prospect of a new entrant into the pallet market but we think there is more than ample opportunity for GKN to compete."
